name: Brickson
description: An iPhone and iPad app that speaks for people living with ALS. Choose a phrase or type a message and it says it aloud, in your own Personal Voice if you have one. Works with touch, Voice Control, Switch Control, head tracking and Eye Tracking.

paragraphs: Brickson (the working name) is an iPhone and iPad app that speaks for people living with ALS. A person chooses a phrase, and the app says it aloud, in their own Personal Voice if they have made one. It is being built to work at every stage of the disease and with every way an Apple device can be controlled: touch, Voice Control, Switch Control, a keyboard, AssistiveTouch with Dwell, head tracking and Eye Tracking.
Everything stays on the device. There are no accounts, no servers, no ads and no analytics.

Status: early. On GitHub's test machines the app builds, opens on an iPad simulator, shows its starter phrases and speaks one when it is chosen. Nobody has run it on a real device yet, and most features are still to come; docs/HANDOFF.md says exactly where things stand.
features: Change project settings in project.yml, not in Xcode's project
